chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Mu'awiyah ibn Shurayh, who said:

'Udhafir asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, while I was with him, about the leftover water of the cat, the sheep, the cow, the camel, the donkey, the horse, the mules, and the beasts of prey: may one drink from it or perform wudu (ablution) from it? He said: Yes, drink from it and perform wudu (ablution). He said: I said to him: The dog? He said: No. I said: Is it not a beast of prey? He said: No, by Allah, it is najis (ritually impure); no, by Allah, it is najis (ritually impure).

key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: the dog, specifically excluded in this ruling
key_terms.سُؤْرِ: leftover water or remaining drink after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: to perform wudu (ablution) with that water

ai.seo_question: Can one drink or perform wudu (ablution) from water touched by animals, especially a dog?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the leftover water from which various animals have drunk. It permits drinking and performing wudu (ablution) from the leftover water of several animals, including beasts of prey, but explicitly excludes the dog and declares it najis (ritually impure).
